revision: 1. Preserve every board object and HUD item, but enlarge the grid substantially, trim its container exactly to the 10-column board, and pull controls/objectives closer to its edges so title/status → board → current objective → controls becomes one compact gameplay group. 2. Make mechanics self-explanatory: redraw two goals to match crate footprints, enlarge the lever with a base and clear state, render a recognizable closed door, and connect lever to door with one matching cable/lock cue. Keep player, crates, goals, lever, and door visually distinct. 3. Establish a shared industrial icon grid and material grammar: one tile gap/border/inset shadow, consistent outline/highlight/shadow across interactables, wood for crates/door, brass for goals/lever, cyan for player. Increase title, HUD, status, and instruction contrast; align both side modules to board grid lines and remove unused outer space. 4. Add authored foundry character through restrained floor wear or heat markings along likely routes and state changes on lever/door, not through extra panel decoration.
conflicts: The full object set and side guidance must remain, while the board needs more dominance; enlarge and tighten the entire gameplay group rather than deleting controls or objectives.
Matched material roles improve mechanic relationships, but goals, lever, and door must remain distinguishable; share brass semantics while keeping unique silhouettes and a direct linkage cue.
Expressive wear can enrich the foundry, but excessive markings would reduce puzzle readability; confine them to subtle route-supporting traces.
rationale: I prioritized visible lever–door and crate–goal relationships, using one industrial asset grammar to improve both clarity and distinctiveness without crowding the grid.
audit_note: Central moderation authored from the task brief, shared r0 screenshot, and all four shared axis critiques only. No FUSED or MAD outputs, generated revisions, HTML variants, or scores were inspected.
